parts.title: The Overrated Art of the Opening Line
parts.directions: Read the passage and choose the best answer (A, B, C, or D) for each question.
passage: Many readers believe that a novel's success rests heavily on its opening line, the single sentence meant to grab attention before anything else happens. Bookstores post lists of the "best first lines in literature," and writing workshops sometimes spend an entire class session on one opening sentence alone. This belief is common, but it may be somewhat misplaced.

A look at well-loved novels complicates the idea. Several classic books open with fairly ordinary sentences that simply state a fact or introduce a character without any dramatic trick. Readers of these books rarely mention the first line as the reason they kept reading; instead, they describe becoming interested gradually, as characters and events built up over several chapters.

Modern publishing has, however, made the opening line matter more than it once did. Online retailers often let shoppers preview only the first page of a book before buying it, so authors and editors now feel pressure to open with something immediately striking — a shocking statement, an unusual image, or a very short, dramatic sentence. **This pressure** can push a writer toward an opening that does not match the calmer tone of the chapters that follow.

None of this means first lines are worthless. A strong opening can set a story's tone efficiently, and a badly written one can certainly make a reader hesitate. Still, few people actually put a book down permanently because of one weak sentence, especially if a friend recommended it or the subject already interests them. Most readers give a book several pages, not one sentence, before deciding whether to continue.

What ultimately keeps someone reading for three hundred pages is not a clever opening but **steady**, consistent quality across the whole book — believable characters, a plot that keeps developing, and prose that stays interesting chapter after chapter. Treating the opening line as the single most important sentence in a novel may distract new writers from the harder, more important work of building a story that holds together from beginning to end.

questions.stem: According to the passage, what do writing workshops sometimes do with a novel's opening line?

options.A: They ignore it completely in favor of studying the ending.
options.B: They ask students to remove the opening line entirely.
options.C: They spend an entire class session focused on one sentence.
options.D: They compare it directly to a bestseller's opening line.

options.A: Opening lines matter far more today than they did in earlier decades.
options.B: A novel's opening line is generally less important than sustained quality throughout.
options.C: Classic novels always open with plain, uninteresting sentences on purpose.
options.D: Publishers should stop allowing shoppers to preview a book's first page.

parts.title: From English Teacher to E-Commerce Pioneer: The Early Career of Jack Ma
parts.directions: Read the passage and choose the best answer (A, B, C, or D) for each question.
passage: Before he became known for building one of the world's largest e-commerce companies, Jack Ma spent years failing at the very jobs that might have seemed like natural stepping stones toward business success. That gap between his early career and his later reputation is, in many ways, more instructive than the outcome itself, since it suggests his path to prominence was shaped as much by repeated rejection as by any early sign of talent.

Ma failed the Chinese college entrance exam twice before finally gaining admission to a teacher-training college on his third attempt, and he was later rejected from dozens of jobs, including, according to widely repeated accounts, a position at a newly opened local KFC. Rather than a technology career, he settled into teaching English at a college in Hangzhou, work that gave him little obvious preparation for the digital economy that would later define his life.

A trip to the United States in the mid-1990s proved unexpectedly **pivotal-** . While there, Ma used the internet for what he later described as the first time, searching for information related to Chinese products and finding almost nothing available online. **That absence**, rather than any abundance of opportunity, appears to have been the detail that convinced him a market existed for connecting Chinese businesses to a global online audience.

His first venture built on this insight, an early online business directory, struggled against bureaucratic obstacles and a telecommunications environment that was not yet equipped for the kind of company he was trying to build. The venture is often described in hindsight as a commercial failure, though some accounts suggest it also functioned as an informal education in exactly which problems a future company would need to solve.

Alibaba itself was founded a few years later, reportedly in Ma's own apartment with a small group of early collaborators, though details of the company's earliest days have been retold so many times, and with so many variations, that separating confirmed fact from company mythology has become genuinely difficult for outside historians. What most accounts agree on is that early funding was **scarce** and that few outside observers expected the venture to succeed.

Looking back at this sequence of setbacks, it becomes difficult to treat Ma's eventual success as a story of steady, predictable rise. It reads instead as a case in which sustained failure across unrelated fields — examinations, employment, an earlier business — arguably built exactly the tolerance for risk and rejection that a later, far riskier venture would require, even though no single failure on its own pointed toward that outcome.

Phương án đúng phải khái quát được hành trình những thất bại sớm của Jack Ma đã định hình con đường thành lập công ty sau này.

parts.title: Why Most Exercise Regimens Fail Before They Begin
parts.directions: Read the passage and choose the best answer (A, B, C, or D) for each question.
passage: Every January, gyms fill with new members whose enthusiasm rarely survives past February, and the conventional explanation for this pattern places blame squarely on the individual: insufficient willpower, poor discipline, competing priorities. This explanation is intuitive, widely repeated, and, according to a growing body of behavioral research, largely incomplete. What actually determines whether a new exercise habit survives its first months has less to do with a person's underlying character than with structural features of the regimen itself — features most people never consciously evaluate before starting.

Early motivation for a new fitness routine is often driven by novelty and identity aspiration — the appeal of becoming, however abstractly imagined, a different kind of person. This initial surge, however, is neurochemically distinct from the mechanisms that sustain long-term habitual behavior. Habits, once established, run largely on automatic cues rather than deliberate motivation; the problem is that most beginner regimens are designed around motivation alone, with no attention paid to building the environmental or contextual triggers that would eventually let the behavior run without conscious effort.

Consider, too, how most regimens define success. Outcome-based goals — losing a specific number of kilograms, reaching a particular strength benchmark — dominate popular fitness culture, in part because they are easy to state and easy to measure retrospectively. What they rarely provide, though, is meaningful feedback in the short term; a person training consistently for three weeks may see no visible change on a scale, and this absence of feedback, rather than any lapse in effort, is frequently what **precipitates** abandonment. Process-based goals, framed around the behavior itself rather than its eventual result, sidestep this problem by offering a form of success — the session was completed — available every single day.

Equally underappreciated is the role of friction, a term researchers use to describe the small, often trivial obstacles standing between intention and action. Whether a gym bag is packed the night before, whether a gym is a five-minute or a forty-minute commute, whether workout clothes are visible or buried in a drawer — **these details**, individually minor, compound into a substantial predictor of adherence. Reducing friction is not a matter of willpower at all; it is closer to environmental design, and regimens that ignore it place an unnecessary and largely avoidable burden on motivation that would otherwise be sufficient.

Social structure complicates the picture further. **[1]** Group classes, fitness challenges, and paid personal training sessions can dramatically boost short-term adherence by supplying external accountability that a solitary regimen lacks. **[2]** Once that external structure disappears — the challenge ends, the class schedule changes, the trainer's contract expires — adherence often collapses just as quickly as it rose, unless an internal sense of identity as someone who exercises has taken root in the meantime. **[3]** This is precisely why regimens built entirely around externally imposed structure, however effective at first, rarely produce **durable** behavior change on their own. **[4]** Sustainable adherence appears to require a period of overlap, during which external accountability and internal identity develop simultaneously rather than sequentially.

None of this implies that willpower plays no role whatsoever; sustaining any new behavior clearly requires some degree of self-directed effort. What the evidence complicates is the assumption that willpower is the primary or even the most significant variable. Regimens engineered around small, easily repeatable process goals, reduced environmental friction, and a deliberate transition from external accountability to internal identity appear, across multiple studies, to produce meaningfully higher adherence rates than those relying on ambition and self-discipline alone — a finding with implications well beyond exercise, for any domain in which a difficult new habit is meant to outlast its initial motivation.

parts.title: Pardons, Parole, and the Unresolved Tension Between Mercy and Deterrence
parts.directions: Read the passage and choose the best answer (A, B, C, or D) for each question.
passage: Executive clemency and parole occupy an uneasy space in criminal justice systems that otherwise pride themselves on procedural consistency, because both mechanisms exist precisely to override the sentence a court has already determined through due process. Not only does this create an obvious tension with the principle that similar offenses should receive similar treatment, but it also forces policymakers to confront, explicitly, a question the sentencing process itself tends to obscure: what, exactly, is punishment supposed to accomplish once the initial verdict has been rendered?

Proponents of robust clemency and parole systems typically appeal to mercy and rehabilitation, arguing that a person's culpability and capacity for harm are not fixed at the moment of sentencing but may shift, sometimes considerably, over years or decades of incarceration. A rigid system that ignores this possibility, the argument runs, risks continuing to punish a person for a version of themselves that may no longer exist — though critics counter that **this framing** assumes a degree of measurable transformation that parole boards are rarely equipped to assess with confidence.

Deterrence theory complicates this picture considerably. If the credible threat of a fixed, predictable sentence is what discourages potential offenders, then a system that regularly commutes or shortens sentences may — depending on how visibly and how often clemency is exercised — undermine the very deterrent effect sentencing was designed to produce. Whether this erosion is significant in practice remains genuinely contested; some researchers argue the deterrent effect of sentence length was always weaker than commonly assumed, in which case clemency's marginal cost to deterrence would be correspondingly small.

Empirical evidence bearing directly on this question is sparser than either side of the debate tends to acknowledge. Recidivism studies comparing paroled and non-paroled populations frequently fail to control adequately for the selection effects built into parole boards' own decisions — boards do not release prisoners at random, but rather select those already judged lowest-risk, which mechanically depresses the recidivism rate among the paroled group regardless of whether parole itself caused any behavioral change. **Disentangling** the effect of parole from the effect of who gets selected for it has proven, in practice, extraordinarily difficult.

A further complication concerns disparity in how clemency power is actually exercised. Analyses of pardon and commutation records in several jurisdictions have found that applicants with greater access to legal representation, media attention, or political connection succeed at markedly higher rates than applicants with comparable case merits but fewer such resources — a pattern that, whatever its cause, sits uneasily beside clemency's stated justification as an act of individualized mercy rather than a privilege extended disproportionately to the well-connected.

None of these complications resolves the underlying tension identified at the outset; if anything, they sharpen it. **[1]** A system that abandons clemency entirely **forecloses** the possibility of correcting sentences that later prove excessive or unjust, a cost difficult to dismiss given how often sentencing itself is later revised on appeal. **[2]** A system that exercises clemency too liberally, or too unevenly, risks eroding both deterrence and public confidence in the fairness of the process. **[3]** Evidence so far offers no reliable formula for locating the point at which one risk begins to outweigh the other. **[4]**

What emerges from the available research, then, is not a resolution but a more precise account of the trade-off itself: mercy and deterrence are not simply opposing values to be balanced by intuition, but forces whose relative weight shifts depending on how a clemency system is administered, who is empowered to exercise it, and how consistently its criteria are applied — variables that differ enough across jurisdictions that a single verdict on clemency's net effect may not be available at all.

- **Affordable:** Có giá cả phải chăng
- **Reliable:** Đáng tin cậy

- Tránh chỉ trình bày một phía hoặc nghiêng hẳn về một quan điểm ngay từ đầu bài, vì đây là lỗi nghiêm trọng trong dạng bài Discussion.

- **Conclusion:** Đưa ra quan điểm cá nhân, tóm tắt. Ví dụ: In conclusion, although sharing one's life online can strengthen connections, I believe people should be mindful of what they post in order to protect their privacy and mental wellbeing.

- **Stay connected:** Duy trì kết nối

- **Preserve memories:** Lưu giữ kỷ niệm

- **Oversharing:** Chia sẻ quá mức
- **Digital footprint:** Dấu vết kỹ thuật số

Questions:

Let’s talk about green spaces

1
Are there many green spaces, such as parks or gardens, in the area where you live?
2
How often do you visit green spaces near your home?
3
Do you think cities should have more green spaces? Why?

Now, let’s talk about food

4
What kind of food do you enjoy eating the most?
5
Do you prefer home-cooked food or food from restaurants?
6
Do you think eating habits have changed a lot compared to the past?
parts.guide_md:
**1. Phân tích đề bài:**
- Phần thi này có **2 chủ đề nhỏ**: **Topic A (Green Spaces)** và **Topic B (Food)**.
- **Topic A (Green Spaces):** Ba câu hỏi đầu kiểm tra khả năng mô tả không gian xanh nơi sinh sống, tần suất ghé thăm, và quan điểm về tầm quan trọng của không gian xanh trong đô thị.
- **Topic B (Food):** Ba câu hỏi sau kiểm tra khả năng nói về sở thích ăn uống, so sánh giữa ăn ở nhà và ăn ngoài, và quan điểm về sự thay đổi thói quen ăn uống theo thời gian.
- Tiêu chí đánh giá gồm **Fluency, Vocabulary, Grammar và Pronunciation**.
- Thời gian Part 1 là **3 phút**, nên dành khoảng 25–35 giây cho mỗi câu hỏi, cân bằng đều giữa hai chủ đề.

**2. Cách xây dựng bố cục khi nói (Organization):**
- Sử dụng cấu trúc **Answer – Reason – Example (ARE)** để trả lời đầy đủ và có chiều sâu.
- **Ví dụ Topic A:** "Yes, there's a small park near my house where I often go jogging in the morning, and it really helps me relax before starting my day."
- **Ví dụ Topic B:** "I really enjoy Vietnamese traditional food, especially noodle soups, because they're both delicious and comforting."
- Luôn tự hỏi Why?/How? để mở rộng câu trả lời, tránh nói quá ngắn.
- Khi chuyển từ Topic A sang Topic B, dùng câu chuyển ý tự nhiên như "Besides enjoying green spaces, I'd also like to share a bit about my eating habits."

**3. Chiến lược đạt điểm cao (Fluency, Vocabulary & Grammar):**
- Dùng **hiện tại đơn** khi mô tả thói quen chung, dùng **so sánh hơn** khi so sánh quá khứ và hiện tại về thói quen ăn uống.
- Nếu bí từ, hãy diễn đạt bằng từ đơn giản hơn thay vì im lặng.
- Từ vựng cho Topic A: a breath of fresh air, urban greenery, reduce air pollution, a place to unwind.
- Từ vựng cho Topic B: a well-balanced meal, home-cooked food, dine out, culinary preferences.
Cụm từ quan trọng nên dùng:
- **a breath of fresh air** (một luồng không khí trong lành)
- **urban greenery** (mảng xanh đô thị)
- **reduce air pollution** (giảm ô nhiễm không khí)
- **a well-balanced meal** (một bữa ăn cân bằng dinh dưỡng)
- **home-cooked food** (đồ ăn tự nấu tại nhà)
- **culinary preferences** (sở thích ẩm thực)
Từ nối khi nói (Linking Words):
- **Firstly** - trước hết, dùng để mở đầu ý.
- **Besides** - bên cạnh đó, dùng để bổ sung ý.
- **For example** - ví dụ như, dùng khi minh họa.
- **However** - tuy nhiên, dùng khi đối chiếu ý kiến.
- **Overall** - nhìn chung, dùng để tổng kết ý.
Cách thể hiện quan điểm tự nhiên:
- **Personally, I think...** Ví dụ: "Personally, I think green spaces are essential for people's mental health in busy cities."
- **In my opinion...** Ví dụ: "In my opinion, home-cooked food is usually healthier than restaurant food."
- **I would say that...** Ví dụ: "I would say that people's eating habits have become more convenience-focused compared to the past."

**4. Các lỗi thường gặp:**
- Trả lời "Yes"/"No" rồi im lặng mà không giải thích thêm - lỗi nghiêm trọng nhất.
- Ở Topic A, chỉ nói tên công viên mà không mô tả hoạt động hay lý do ghé thăm.
- Ở Topic B, chỉ liệt kê tên món ăn mà không giải thích lý do yêu thích.
- Dùng sai thì khi so sánh thói quen ăn uống giữa quá khứ và hiện tại.

**5. Chiến lược xử lý khi bí ý hoặc quên từ:**
- Dùng câu đệm: "That's an interesting question, let me think for a second."
- Nếu quên từ, hãy mô tả khái niệm bằng từ đơn giản hơn.
- Với Topic A, nếu bí ý, hãy mô tả một buổi đi dạo công viên gần đây của bạn.
- Với Topic B, nếu bí ý, hãy kể về một món ăn cụ thể bạn thường ăn.

**6. Tư duy làm bài nói:**
- Coi đây như một cuộc trò chuyện thân mật với giám khảo, không phải bài kiểm tra căng thẳng.

You saw your friend cheating during an exam and need to decide how to react.

You are considering the following options:

Option 1: Ignore what you saw and say nothing
Option 2: Report the incident to the teacher
Option 3: Talk directly to your friend about it

Choose the best option and explain your reasons.
parts.guide_md:
**1. Phân tích đề bài:**
- Đây là dạng **Solution Discussion**. Bạn cần chọn cách xử lý phù hợp nhất khi phát hiện bạn mình gian lận trong kỳ thi, trong ba lựa chọn: phớt lờ, báo giáo viên, hoặc nói chuyện trực tiếp với bạn đó.
- Ba lựa chọn khác biệt về mức độ can thiệp, tính công bằng, và ảnh hưởng đến mối quan hệ bạn bè.
- Thời gian là **4 phút**; cần phân tích cả ba phương án trước khi đưa ra kết luận.

**2. Cách xây dựng bố cục khi nói (Organization):**
- Sử dụng cấu trúc **Introduction – Comparison – Conclusion** để trình bày mạch lạc.
- **Option 1 (phớt lờ):** "Ignoring the situation might avoid conflict in the short term, but it could make you feel guilty for not doing anything about dishonest behavior."
- **Option 2 (báo giáo viên):** "Reporting the incident to the teacher ensures fairness for other students, although it might damage your friendship if your friend feels betrayed."
- **Option 3 (nói chuyện trực tiếp):** "Talking directly to your friend allows you to address the issue personally and give them a chance to correct their behavior before it becomes more serious."
- Nên neo lập luận vào giá trị công bằng trong thi cử và tầm quan trọng của tình bạn.
- Dùng từ nối tương phản như "however", "whereas" để chuyển giữa ưu và nhược điểm của từng lựa chọn.

**3. Chiến lược đạt điểm cao (Fluency, Vocabulary & Grammar):**
- Liên kết các lựa chọn với nhau thay vì nói tách rời, ví dụ: "Unlike simply ignoring it, talking directly to your friend addresses the issue while preserving the relationship."
- Dùng modal verbs (would, could, should) khi giả định và đề xuất giải pháp.
- Paraphrase "cheating" bằng "academic dishonesty"; paraphrase "tell the teacher" bằng "report the incident". Cụm từ quan trọng nên dùng:
- **academic dishonesty** (gian lận trong học tập)
- **a sense of fairness** (tinh thần công bằng)
- **damage the friendship** (làm tổn hại tình bạn)
- **address the issue personally** (giải quyết vấn đề một cách cá nhân)
- **serious consequences** (những hậu quả nghiêm trọng)
- **a moral dilemma** (một tình huống khó xử về đạo đức)
Từ nối khi nói (Linking Words):
- **Compared with** - so với, dùng khi so sánh hai lựa chọn.
- **Whereas** - trong khi đó, dùng để đối lập.
- **Nevertheless** - tuy nhiên, dùng để chuyển ý ngược lại.
- **Taking everything into account** - xét tất cả các yếu tố, dùng trước kết luận.
- **In terms of** - xét về mặt, dùng khi so sánh theo tiêu chí cụ thể.
Cách thể hiện quan điểm tự nhiên:
- **If I had to choose, I would go with...** Ví dụ: "If I had to choose, I would go with talking to my friend directly first, before considering any other action."
- **I'm more inclined towards...** Ví dụ: "I'm more inclined towards a private conversation rather than reporting
immediately."
- **All things considered...** Ví dụ: "All things considered, speaking to my friend directly seems like the most respectful first step."

**4. Các lỗi thường gặp:**
- Chỉ khen lựa chọn mình chọn mà không phân tích nhược điểm của nó.
- Lặp lại từ "good"/"bad" quá nhiều thay vì dùng tính từ học thuật hơn.

• To begin with - trước hết, dùng để mở đầu nhánh đầu tiên.
• Moving on to - chuyển sang, dùng khi chuyển nhánh ý.
• Furthermore - hơn nữa, dùng để bổ sung ý.
• In addition to that - thêm vào đó, dùng để mở rộng ý.
• To sum up - tóm lại, dùng khi kết luận.
Cách thể hiện quan điểm tự nhiên:
• I firmly believe that... Ví dụ: "I firmly believe that cashless payment has made everyday transactions much more
convenient."
• It seems to me that... Ví dụ: "It seems to me that more people are choosing digital payment over carrying cash."
• What strikes me most is... Ví dụ: "What strikes me most is how quickly a payment can be completed with just a scan
of a QR code."
4. Gợi ý trả lời câu hỏi follow-up:
• "Do you think cashless payment will completely replace cash in the future?" - Có thể, vì ngày càng nhiều người trẻ
ưa chuộng sự tiện lợi của thanh toán điện tử, mặc dù tiền mặt vẫn cần thiết ở một số khu vực nông thôn.
• "What are some risks associated with cashless payment methods?" - Một số rủi ro bao gồm bị đánh cắp thông tin
tài khoản, lừa đảo trực tuyến, hoặc sự cố kỹ thuật khiến giao dịch không thực hiện được.
• "How has cashless payment changed shopping habits in your country?" - Người tiêu dùng hiện nay mua sắm nhanh
hơn và thường xuyên hơn nhờ việc thanh toán chỉ mất vài giây qua ứng dụng di động.
5. Các lỗi thường gặp:
• Liệt kê lợi ích mà không giải thích cụ thể - luôn cần đưa ví dụ minh họa.
• Quên nhánh ý kiến cá nhân - nên chuẩn bị trước nhánh thứ tư này.
• Nói quá dài ở phần mở đầu khiến không còn thời gian trả lời câu hỏi follow-up.
6. Chiến lược xử lý khi bí ý hoặc quên từ:
• Neo vào trải nghiệm cá nhân, như một lần thanh toán bằng ứng dụng ngân hàng hoặc ví điện tử, khi bí ý.
• Câu chờ ý học thuật: "That is an interesting point. If we look at it from an economic perspective..."
• Dùng từ đồng nghĩa hoặc mô tả đơn giản nếu quên từ vựng chuyên môn.
7. Tư duy làm bài nói:
• Suy nghĩ cân bằng giữa lợi ích và rủi ro của thanh toán không tiền mặt, tránh chỉ nói một chiều.
• Sự mạch lạc và logic trong cách triển khai ý là yếu tố quyết định điểm số.
• Luôn giữ giọng điệu tự nhiên, tránh đọc thuộc lòng như một bài văn mẫu.
